steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren wound the clockwork every night at dusk, same as she had for forty years.

The storms didn't scare her anymore. Neither did the loneliness.

What scared her was the evening the mechanism finally broke — gears stripped, lamp dark — and she stood at the top of the tower with nothing but a lantern and her own two arms, swinging the light back and forth through the howling black.

In the morning, a fishing boat anchored safely in the harbor.

The captain waved up at the lighthouse.

She waved back.

That was enough.
